assessments.reasoning: Paragraph 11/3 assigns reverse creation order to the master’s declaration-created objects. Paragraph 11.1/3 establishes the distinct collection rule with arbitrary order among the objects in it.

challenge.method: Compare declaration-created objects, a collection object, member objects and the nonderived access type, and the storage subpool permission in §7.6.1(20.2/3).
challenge.results: A collection can occupy a position in the master sequence while its members follow their own rule. An explicit deallocation can remove a member. Subpools have a separate permission with an alternate as-if point. Composite component order also follows its own clause.

limitations: The reverse-order rule is not a universal rule for objects within an access-type collection or for components of one composite object. Explicit deallocation and object accessibility have separate conditions.
Exact unannotated Ada 2022 manual edition only. Runtime implementations and other editions require separate evidence.
